MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If a = 5, what is the value of a + 7? (1 mark)
   A. 35
   B. 57
   C. 2
   D. 12

2. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 2/4
   B. 3 3/4
   C. 2 4/4
   D. 2 3/4

3. Round 831 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 820
   B. 800
   C. 840
   D. 830

4. What is 3.4 m in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 3,400 cm
   B. 304 cm
   C. 34 cm
   D. 340 cm

5. Which is the smallest number: 605, 560, 650, 506? (1 mark)
   A. 650
   B. 605
   C. 560
   D. 506

6. What is 3/4 of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 9
   C. 12
   D. 3

7. Kip faces East and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. East
   C. North
   D. West

8. What is 5 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 6 kg
   B. 6 1/2 kg
   C. 6 1/4 kg
   D. 5 3/4 kg

9. A rectangle is made of 7 rows with 9 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 70 square units
   B. 32 square units
   C. 16 square units
   D. 63 square units

10. You face the door and make a half turn. What do you face now? (1 mark)
   A. The door
   B. The left wall only
   C. The back wall
   D. The ceiling

11. A remainder must always be (1 mark)
   A. bigger than the divisor
   B. smaller than the divisor
   C. equal to the divisor
   D. equal to the quotient

12. A rectangle is made of 12 rows with 7 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 19 square units
   B. 84 square units
   C. 96 square units
   D. 38 square units

13. The relationship between metres and centimetres is (1 mark)
   A. 1 cm = 100 m
   B. 1 m = 10 cm
   C. 1 m = 100 cm
   D. 1 m = 1,000 cm

14. One layer of a cuboid has 15 blocks and there are 3 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 42 blocks
   B. 18 blocks
   C. 45 blocks
   D. 60 blocks

15. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. How many are football or swimming together? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 8
   C. 7
   D. 6

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Start at 1,500 and add 1,000 each time to write a pattern of five numbers. State the rule. (3 marks)

17. Describe how to make a 1/2 kg mass from sand using a 1 kg mass and a beam balance. (4 marks)

18. A trader sold goods worth Ksh 3,568 on Monday and Ksh 2,276 on Tuesday. (a) Find the total. (b) Estimate the total by rounding each amount to the nearest ten. (c) How far is the estimate from the exact total? (5 marks)

19. Explain what the 0 in 4.05 shows and say how 4.05 is different from 4.5. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 12
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 12.

2. D — 2 3/4
   11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3. The whole number is 2 and the fraction is 3/4, so 11/4 = 2 3/4.

3. D — 830
   Look at the ones digit 1. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 831 rounds to 830.

4. D — 340 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 3.4 m in centimetres is 340 cm.

5. D — 506
   Compare the digits from the left. The smallest number is 506.

6. B — 9
   12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 3 × 3 = 9. So 3/4 of 12 is 9.

7. D — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. East followed by a half turn gives West.

8. A — 6 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 5 1/2 kg + 1/2 kg = 6 kg.

9. D — 63 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 7 × 9 = 63 square units.

10. C — The back wall
   A half turn takes you to face the opposite way.

11. B — smaller than the divisor
   If the remainder were as big as the divisor, another whole group could still be made.

12. B — 84 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 12 × 7 = 84 square units.

13. C — 1 m = 100 cm
   There are 100 centimetres in one metre.

14. C — 45 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 15 × 3 = 45 blocks.

15. D — 6
   5 + 1 = 6.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,500, 2,500, 3,500, 4,500, 5,500. Rule: add 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for five correct terms (1 mark for three or four).

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: Balance a bag of sand against the 1 kg mass. Share the sand equally into two bags, checking with the balance that they are level. Each bag is 1/2 kg.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for balancing sand with 1 kg, 1 mark for sharing into two bags, 1 mark for checking they balance, 1 mark for stating each is 1/2 kg.

18. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 5,844 (b) 3,570 + 2,280 = Ksh 5,850 (c) 6 shillings more than the exact total
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact total with regrouping, 1 mark for both rounded numbers, 1 mark for the estimate 5,850, 1 mark for the difference 5,850 − 5,844 = 6.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: The 0 shows that there are no tenths. 4.05 is 4 ones and 5 hundredths; 4.5 is 4 ones and 5 tenths, which is bigger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of zero, 1 mark for each correct reading.
